sources.name: SAM.gov – Contract Opportunities
sources.apiDetails: Get Opportunities Public API v2: https://api.sam.gov/opportunities/v2/search (free API key from SAM.gov Account Details)
sources.mechanisms: Contracts, BAAs, CSOs, RFIs / sources sought, special notices; most DoD/IC OT, SBIR and marketplace notices
sources.notes: Primary feed. DARPA, IARPA, DIA, DIU CSO, Tradewinds and IARPA Marketplace notices all post here — filter by agency/office code.

sources.name: SAM.gov – Assistance Listings
sources.apiDetails: SAM.gov Assistance Listings Public API (same SAM.gov key)
sources.mechanisms: Catalog of every federal assistance program (grants, loans, cooperative agreements) by Assistance Listing Number (ALN/CFDA)
sources.notes: Program catalog, not individual NOFOs. Use it to map which programs fit before watching Grants.gov.

sources.name: Grants.gov
sources.apiDetails: search2 + fetchOpportunity REST — POST https://api.grants.gov/v1/api/search2 — no key required; daily XML extract also available
sources.mechanisms: Grants, cooperative agreements and forecasted NOFOs from civilian agencies and DoD research offices (ONR, ARO, AFOSR, CDMRP)
sources.notes: Built into the scanner: keyword searches plus every open listing at the priority agencies. Best free grant feed. Covers NSF, NIH, DOE, NIST, NOAA, USDA, EDA and most DoD basic-research BAAs.

sources.name: Simpler.Grants.gov
sources.apiDetails: REST: POST https://api.simpler.grants.gov/v1/opportunities/search (X-API-Key header); bulk extracts endpoint for full exports
sources.mechanisms: Same Grants.gov opportunity catalog with modernized search
sources.notes: Cleaner JSON than legacy Grants.gov — good choice for dashboard ingestion. Search capped at 10,000 results per query.

sources.name: SBIR.gov
sources.apiDetails: https://api.www.sbir.gov/public/api/solicitations (JSON/XML; keyword, agency, open/closed filters); award bulk downloads refreshed monthly
sources.mechanisms: SBIR/STTR solicitations and topics from all participating agencies; award and company data
sources.notes: Topics are copies and may lag — confirm on the agency portal (e.g., DSIP) before bidding.

sources.name: Challenge.gov
sources.apiDetails: No public API documented — monitor site / sign up for updates
sources.mechanisms: Federal prize competitions and challenges (America COMPETES and other authorities)
sources.notes: Central hub for federal prize competitions; some DoD prizes (xTech, DIU, AFWERX) are hosted on their own sites instead.

sources.name: GSA Acquisition Gateway – Forecast of Contract Opportunities
sources.apiDetails: Acquisition Gateway Listings API listed on open.gsa.gov; forecast also downloadable
sources.mechanisms: Multi-agency procurement forecasts (mostly civilian agencies)
sources.notes: Coverage varies by agency; DoD and IC forecasts are generally not here.

sources.name: USAspending.gov
sources.mechanisms: Award history for contracts, grants and OTs (who won, how much) — not open opportunities
sources.notes: Connected for past awards: every opportunity's Past awards section comes from here (matched by Assistance Listing). Use to profile sponsors, incumbents and spending trends by office.

sources.name: Federal Register
sources.parentAgency: NARA / Office of the Federal Register
sources.mechanisms: NOFO notices, program rules, new authorities, some BAAs and prize announcements
sources.notes: Good early signal for new programs before NOFOs post.

sources.name: FedConnect
sources.mechanisms: Grant and contract postings / submission for DOE and some other agencies
sources.notes: Many DOE awards are administered here after selection.

sources.name: DARPA
sources.apiDetails: No DARPA API; solicitations post to SAM.gov and Grants.gov — pull via those APIs (agency filter: DARPA)
sources.mechanisms: Broad Agency Announcements, Research Announcements, SBIR/STTR topics, Other Transactions, prize challenges
sources.focusAreas: Office-wide BAAs take any idea in each office's lane. IPTO: information processing, AI, cyber, complex software (replaced the I2O office-wide BAA in June 2026). DSO: novel basic/applied science and studies. TTO: tactical systems and platforms.
sources.unsolicited: Send an abstract under the matching office-wide BAA, ideally after talking to the PM: IPTO HR001126S0011 (open to Jun 22, 2027); DSO HR001126S0015 (abstracts to Aug 27, 2027); TTO Office-Wide BAA (amended Feb 2026).
sources.cadence: Office-wide BAAs reissued about yearly; program BAAs post monthly on SAM.gov.
sources.notes: The examples in your notes (Albatross UAS, Intrinsic Market Resilience, Atomically Precise Molecules, Flexoelectric RFI) were not re-verified — check the live list.

sources.name: DoD SBIR/STTR – Defense SBIR/STTR Innovation Portal (DSIP)
sources.apiDetails: No documented public API; topics mirrored in SBIR.gov API; DSIP Listserv email alerts
sources.mechanisms: SBIR/STTR BAAs and CSOs; topics released monthly (first Wednesday) across 14 DoD components
sources.notes: ~$2B/yr combined SBIR/STTR budget. Proposals must be submitted in DSIP.

sources.name: Defense Innovation Unit (DIU)
sources.apiDetails: No API; interest-form email alerts; umbrella CSO HQ0845-20-S-C001 on SAM.gov
sources.mechanisms: Commercial Solutions Openings → prototype OTs (10 USC 4022); prize challenges (10 USC 4025)
sources.notes: Often awards within 60–90 days; open to U.S. and international vendors.

sources.name: CDAO Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace
sources.apiDetails: No API; SAM.gov special notice W519TC-23-S-CTSM (Rev. 10.0 effective 5/1/2026)
sources.parentAgency: DoD CDAO (marketplace manager: Applied Research Institute)
sources.mechanisms: Open-call video-pitch CSO; solutions rated 'Awardable' can be bought through rapid acquisition pathways (AI/ML, data, digital)
sources.notes: Same model IARPA adopted for its Solutions Marketplace.

sources.name: AFWERX / SpaceWERX
sources.apiDetails: No API; SBIR topics via DSIP / SBIR.gov
sources.mechanisms: SBIR/STTR open topics (via DSIP), TACFI/STRATFI matching funds, challenges and prizes

sources.name: Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) & AFOSR
sources.apiDetails: No API; BAAs on Grants.gov / SAM.gov
sources.mechanisms: Open BAAs for research grants and contracts, OTs, SBIR
sources.focusAreas: AFOSR Research Interests BAA FA9550-26-S-0001 (posted Jun 2026): Engineering & Complex Systems, Information Networks, Physical Sciences, Bio-Cognitive, aligned to FY2027 R&D priorities. AFRL Information Directorate (Rome) open BAAs/ARAs: Resilient Analytic Platforms for Intelligence, SIFTER (SIGINT exploitation & reporting), GeoPEX (GEOINT processing), SIETE (signals exploitation), ultra-broadband THz radio, cyberspace operations for tactical engagement; CHEERS CSO.
sources.unsolicited: White paper to the AFOSR program officer for the topic at any time under the open BAA. For Rome, white papers under the open BAA/ARA per the AFRL BAA Guide for Industry.
sources.cadence: AFOSR BAA reissued yearly (June). AFRL Small Business publishes a monthly 'AFRL Announcements' list of open BAAs.
sources.notes: AFOSR Research Interests BAA is the main basic-research grant vehicle.

sources.name: DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory (incl. Army Research Office)
sources.mechanisms: ARL BAA for foundational research (grants, cooperative agreements, contracts); ARO BAA
sources.focusAreas: ARL BAA for Foundational Research (W911NF-23-S-0001) keeps its topic list on the ARL website. 2026 ARL calls stress DoD critical tech areas incl. Contested Logistics, Quantum & Battlefield Information Dominance (Q-BID), Scaled Directed Energy, Scaled Hypersonics. ARO + NSA QuantumEAGLe initiative for the quantum industry.
sources.unsolicited: Preliminary inquiry or white paper to the ARL/ARO topic POC at any time under the open BAA.
sources.cadence: Topics updated on the ARL website as needed — check monthly.

sources.name: Army xTech / Army Applications Laboratory
sources.mechanisms: Prize competitions (xTechSearch and topic contests); AAL CSOs/OTs
sources.notes: AAL: https://aal.army

sources.name: Office of Naval Research (ONR) & NavalX
sources.mechanisms: ONR Long Range BAA (grants/contracts), Navy SBIR/STTR, NavalX Tech Bridges
sources.focusAreas: 2026 S&T Strategy (Jul 24, 2026): fund 'Only ONR' naval-unique problems, require a credible transition path, use AI to speed discovery. Topic special notices under the Long Range BAA (e.g., Communications & Networking, ONR 311). Navy ManTech sBAA N00014-26-S-B002 (Jul 2026) for shipbuilding/maintenance manufacturing tech.
sources.unsolicited: White paper to the ONR program officer under the Long Range BAA (N00014-25-S-B001, amended May 2026); attend ONR Innovation Industry Days.
sources.cadence: Long Range BAA yearly; topic special notices throughout the year.

sources.name: Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA)
sources.mechanisms: Basic research BAA (grants), contracts, SBIR
sources.focusAreas: Fundamental Research to Counter WMD BAA (HDTRA1-25-S-0001, open through Sep 30, 2034): current emphasis Thrust 1, fundamental science for chem/bio defense, topics B1–B6 (Jan 2026). Also R&D Innovations BAA HDTRA1-22-S-0003, CB Technologies BAA HDTRA1-22-S-0002, Strategic Trends Research Initiative HDTRA1-24-S-0003; Vulcan SOF 2026 technology scouting.
sources.unsolicited: Pre-application white paper (DTRA prefers these) under the matching BAA; non-fundamental ideas go to the R&D Innovations BAA via dtrasubmission.net.
sources.cadence: New topic sets released by BAA amendment, roughly 1–2 per year.

sources.name: CDMRP / Defense Health Agency
sources.apiDetails: No direct API; NOFOs on Grants.gov
sources.mechanisms: Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program grants; DHA SBIR

sources.name: USSOCOM (SOF AT&L)
sources.mechanisms: SOCOM BAA, CSOs, OTs; works heavily through SOFWERX (see PIAs)

sources.name: Office of Strategic Capital (OSC)
sources.mechanisms: Direct loans and loan guarantees for critical-technology supply chains

sources.name: MITRE AiDA – Existing OT Consortia list
sources.mechanisms: Official DoD list of OT consortia (required by Sec. 833, P.L. 116-283)
sources.notes: Updated annually; page shows sponsor, manager and membership fee for each consortium.

sources.name: IARPA – BAAs & Research Programs
sources.apiDetails: No API; solicitations post to SAM.gov (ODNI)
sources.mechanisms: Program BAAs, RFIs, prize challenges, research OTs
sources.focusAreas: Research run by the Office of Analysis and the Office of Collection. Five new programs announced Apr 29, 2026 — ARCADE, COSMIC, DECIPHER, LOCUS, MOVES — on insights from geospatial imagery, circuit design, linguistic trends and open-source video. Featured programs: Amon-Hen, FELIX, SILMARILS, TEI-REX, MicroE4AI.
sources.unsolicited: Seedlings: short high-risk efforts, typically 9–12 months and under $1M — pitch to the relevant PM. Answer RFIs and attend Proposers' Days, which come before new BAAs.
sources.cadence: RFIs and Proposers' Days several times a year; new programs announced in batches.
sources.notes: BENGAL, HAYSTAC, WRIVA etc. are research programs — most are in execution, not open calls. Watch the open-BAAs page for new starts.

sources.name: IARPA Solutions Marketplace
sources.parentAgency: ODNI / IARPA (marketplace manager: Applied Research Institute)
sources.mechanisms: Open-call OT: 5-minute video pitch + submission form + 5 slides; 'Awardable' solutions listed 24 months for any IC/federal buyer
sources.focusAreas: Strategic topic areas: Secure Communications; Cyber & AI Security; Automating the Business of R&D.
sources.unsolicited: This is itself an open call: 5-minute video + submission form + 5 slides.
sources.notes: Rolling monthly cut-offs Aug 1, 2026 – Jul 31, 2027. Topics include Secure Communications, Cyber & AI Security, Automating the Business of R&D.

sources.name: In-Q-Tel
sources.mechanisms: Strategic venture investment and technology work programs for the IC
sources.focusAreas: May 2026 strategy shift to fewer, larger bets in autonomy, contested logistics and critical infrastructure. Technology areas include sensors, manufacturing & energy, trusted infrastructure, biomedical. Oct 2026 formal tech-scouting deal with DoD around its six Critical Technology Areas (AI, biomanufacturing, directed energy, hypersonics, quantum & information tech, contested logistics).
sources.unsolicited: No solicitation — pitch IQT directly (venture-backed companies; work programs plus equity).
sources.cadence: Continuous; strategy changes announced ad hoc.

sources.name: NSA Acquisition Resource Center (ARC)
sources.apiDetails: No API; login required (not reachable from government computers)
sources.mechanisms: Business registry and acquisition information; forecasts and opportunities after registration
sources.focusAreas: Seven mission-oriented research areas: Mathematics; Laboratory for Advanced Cybersecurity Research (automated network defense, trusted HW/SW, formal methods, cyber threat-intel tools); Laboratory for Physical Sciences (quantum & HPC, advanced manufacturing, sensing); Lab for Telecommunication Sciences; Computer & Analytic Sciences; Innovation; Research & Technology Applications.
sources.unsolicited: NSA formally accepts unsolicited proposals under its published guidance (submitted by mail). Also the NSA Industry Engagement Questionnaire, the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center, and Technology Transfer licensing.
sources.cadence: Research areas are stable; check the ARC for current needs.
sources.notes: Registration required to do business with NSA.

sources.name: NRO Acquisition Research Center (ARC) / ACE
sources.mechanisms: IC acquisition portal, classified reading room info, industry overview briefings, subcontracting registry
sources.focusAreas: Aug 27, 2026 priorities: solutions that scale into missions, speed/agility to reprioritize, hybrid (traditional + proliferated) architecture, AI-enabled data processing at scale, data delivery. DII areas of interest: apertures, communications, remote sensing, satellite system design, sense-making, other disruptive concepts. Also the Architecture After Next open BAA and Strategic Commercial Enhancements BAA framework.
sources.unsolicited: Director's Innovation Initiative: yearly BAA + Government Sources Sought Announcement on the ARC, awards up to $500K for about 9 months (DII@nro.mil). Architecture After Next open BAA on the ARC.
sources.cadence: DII yearly (spring); new commercial focus areas about yearly.
sources.notes: The ACE operates the ARC; also used by other IC agencies (e.g., NGA).

sources.name: Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)
sources.apiDetails: No API; pull via SAM.gov API — Federal Organization code 97DL (Virginia Contracting Activity, HHM402)
sources.mechanisms: Annual consolidated procurement forecast (SAM.gov special notice); Virginia Contracting Activity solicitations; OSBP small-business outreach
sources.notes: FY25 forecast was posted in 2024; a July 2026 DIA special notice (DF-0001-26) covers consolidation/bundling — check SAM.gov for the FY26/27 forecast.

sources.name: DIA – NeedipeDIA (Innovation Office)
sources.apiDetails: No API; unclassified white papers to Ideas2Action@dodiis.mil (classified: Ideas2Action@coe.ic.gov); BAA/CSO notices on SAM.gov
sources.mechanisms: Open BAA/CSO white papers answering DIA's posted mission needs; Innovation Office routes each paper to the matching DIA office; innovation industry days
sources.focusAreas: 10 mission themes (list 'updated frequently'): AI/ML for business ops & finished intel; counterintelligence indications & warning; weapon-system collection & analysis; biometrics, space & detection; mission support & data management; emerging tech for rapid transition & advanced comms; adaptive human performance; mission analysis & reporting systems; quantum for decision advantage; novel/experimental tech.
sources.unsolicited: Open BAA HHM402-23-S-0001 and Open CSO HHM402-23-SC-0002 — cite the need in your white paper; questions to Ideas2Action@dodiis.mil.
sources.cadence: Needs list updated frequently — check monthly.
sources.notes: OSBP says the Innovation Office responds within 30 days. NeedipeDIA has also carried DIA Mentor-Protégé and MASINT research calls.

sources.name: DIA – Procurement Forecast & CFO Acquisition Industry Days
sources.apiDetails: No API of its own; query SAM.gov API for special notices from Federal Organization 97DL
sources.mechanisms: Procurement forecast posted as an attachment to SAM.gov special notices for the quarterly CFO acquisition industry days; RFIs and sources-sought notices
sources.notes: DIA says forecasts can change with mission needs. OSBP calls RFI/sources-sought responses the best way to get in front of program offices.

sources.name: DIA – Office of Small Business Programs (briefings & set-asides)
sources.apiDetails: No API; register through the OSBP page; contact by email
sources.mechanisms: 'Introduction to DIA' briefings (2nd & 4th Wednesday monthly), 30-minute one-on-one virtual capabilities briefings, monthly virtual outreach and matchmaking; 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB/EDWOSB, HUBZone set-asides
sources.notes: Most DIA contracts need a Top Secret facility clearance at proposal; DIA suggests finding a prime to sponsor the clearance. OSBP is moving to monthly group meetings instead of one-on-ones.

sources.name: DIA – Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 3 (SIA 3)
sources.apiDetails: No API; task orders competed among the 16 prime holders — others enter as subcontractors
sources.mechanisms: Multiple-award IDIQ for intelligence analysis and analytic enabling: Analysis, Sciences, Engineering, Analytic Enabling, CI/HUMINT/Collections
sources.notes: Awarded 2019 to 16 primes (6 small); $17.1B combined ceiling; runs through Aug 2029.

sources.name: DIA – Solutions for the IT Enterprise III (SITE III)
sources.apiDetails: No API; task orders among prime holders — subcontract through primes
sources.mechanisms: 10-year multiple-award IDIQ for IT design, development, fielding and sustainment for DIA and NGA
sources.notes: Estimated $12.6B total value across awardees.

sources.name: DoDIIS Worldwide Conference
sources.mechanisms: Annual DIA CIO conference on IT challenges facing intelligence mission users
sources.notes: Good venue to meet SITE III primes and DIA IT program offices.

sources.name: DoD Mentor-Protégé Program (DIA participates)
sources.mechanisms: Mentor-protégé agreements pairing large primes with small businesses; DIA runs a version tailored to its needs

sources.name: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA)
sources.mechanisms: NGA BAA (research grants/contracts), contracts via SAM.gov, NGA Accelerator
sources.focusAreas: BIG-ST BAA (HM047623BAA0001) domains: Foundational GEOINT, Advanced Phenomenologies, Analytic Technologies. Topic 7 LASER (lidar analysis for surface & environmental reconnaissance) opened Oct 1, 2026. The BAA's publication period ends Dec 14, 2026 — watch for a successor.
sources.unsolicited: Respond to BIG-ST topic calls; questions to BIGSTBAA@nga.mil.
sources.cadence: New topic calls every few months.

sources.name: National Science Foundation (NSF)
sources.apiDetails: No opportunities API — NOFOs via Grants.gov API. NSF Award Search API (https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards.json, no key) covers awards only
sources.mechanisms: Grants, cooperative agreements, fellowships, SBIR/STTR (America's Seed Fund)
sources.notes: NSF Award Search is connected for past awards (abstracts on each NSF opportunity). Research.gov is the proposal-submission system. Deadlines in your notes (Robotics anytime, MRI, STC) were not re-verified. Team note: From the team's Grant Checker site list. NSF listings also reach Grants.gov, which is already scanned.

sources.name: National Institutes of Health (NIH)
sources.apiDetails: RSS feed: https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/newsfeed/fundingopps.xml; NOFOs via Grants.gov API; NIH RePORTER API for awards
sources.mechanisms: Research grants, SBIR/STTR, contracts, Common Fund OTs

sources.name: ARPA-H
sources.mechanisms: Innovative Solutions Openings / BAAs, Other Transactions, prizes

sources.name: BARDA / DRIVe
sources.mechanisms: BARDA BAA, EZ-BAA, OTs, BARDA Ventures
sources.notes: DRIVe: https://drive.hhs.gov

sources.name: DOE Office of Science & program offices
sources.mechanisms: FOAs (grants / cooperative agreements), SBIR/STTR, national-lab partnerships
sources.notes: Office of Science grants: https://science.osti.gov/grants

sources.name: ARPA-E
sources.mechanisms: FOAs, OTs, SBIR/STTR
sources.notes: Team note: From the team's Grant Checker site list.

sources.name: NASA
sources.apiDetails: No API; acquisition forecast searchable online at https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/forecast/
sources.mechanisms: ROSES and other solicitations via NSPIRES, SBIR/STTR, prize competitions, agency-wide acquisition forecast

sources.name: DHS Science & Technology (SVIP, LRBAA)
sources.mechanisms: Silicon Valley Innovation Program (phased OTs), Long Range BAA, SBIR, Commercial Solutions Opening pilot

sources.name: DHS Procurement Forecast (APFS → 4SITE)
sources.apiDetails: No API; Excel/PDF downloads of the full forecast on DHS.gov; viewing at apfs-era.dhs.gov
sources.mechanisms: Forecast of anticipated DHS contract actions over $350K; email alerts by NAICS, vehicle, dollar range, set-aside
sources.notes: APFS stopped taking new forecasts Oct 30, 2026. Replacement is 4SITE. Alerts expected to resume ~Dec 9, 2026.

sources.name: FEMA / CISA grants
sources.apiDetails: NOFOs via Grants.gov API; OpenFEMA API for award data
sources.mechanisms: Preparedness grants (incl. State & Local Cybersecurity Grant Program), contracts

sources.name: NIST (incl. CHIPS, MEP)
sources.mechanisms: Grants, cooperative agreements, SBIR, prize competitions

sources.name: NOAA
sources.mechanisms: Grants, SBIR, Other Transactions (15 USC 8531)

sources.name: Economic Development Administration (EDA)
sources.mechanisms: Tech Hubs, Build to Scale and economic-development grants

sources.name: USDA (NIFA, SBIR)
sources.mechanisms: Research and extension grants, SBIR/STTR

sources.name: Department of Transportation
sources.mechanisms: Discretionary grants, SBIR (Volpe)

sources.name: EPA
sources.mechanisms: Grants, SBIR

sources.name: DOJ (NIJ / OJP) + DOJ procurement forecast
sources.mechanisms: NIJ research grants (JustGrants), DOJ forecast of contracting opportunities dashboard
sources.notes: NIJ funding: https://nij.ojp.gov/funding

sources.name: Small Business Administration (SBA)
sources.apiDetails: No API of its own beyond SBIR.gov
sources.mechanisms: SBIR/STTR policy, FAST and Growth Accelerator Fund awards, SBIC investment, loan programs

sources.name: Dept. of Education – IES
sources.mechanisms: Education research grants

sources.name: DEFENSEWERX (DWX)
sources.mechanisms: PIA umbrella for innovation hubs; challenges, tech sprints, assessment events, prize events — PIAs with DoD, DOE and DHS
sources.notes: Hubs include SOFWERX and Doolittle Institute.

sources.name: SOFWERX
sources.mechanisms: Assessment events, rapid-prototyping events, prize challenges for USSOCOM

sources.name: Doolittle Institute
sources.mechanisms: Tech transfer, challenges and collaboration with AFRL Munitions Directorate (Eglin AFB)

sources.name: National Security Innovation Network (NSIN)

sources.notes: Current program status not re-verified — confirm before relying on it.

sources.mechanisms: Technology transition, manufacturing and design review, technology scouting

sources.name: VT-ARC – Basic Research Innovation Collaboration Center (BRICC)

sources.mechanisms: Armaments and ordnance prototypes

sources.notes: From the team's Grant Checker site list.

sources.notes: From the team's Grant Checker site list.

reviewNotes.said: Moved to https://era-apfs.dhs.gov in Nov 2026; subscribe for automated notifications
reviewNotes.found: Reporting gives the viewing URL as apfs-era.dhs.gov (word order reversed) plus a DHS.gov landing page. APFS stopped taking new forecasts Oct 30, 2026; the replacement system is called 4SITE; existing alert subscriptions are expected to carry over and resume ~Dec 9, 2026. Excel/PDF downloads continue. No API.
reviewNotes.action: Fix the URL; re-check alerts after Dec 9; plan to scrape the Excel download for the dashboard.

reviewNotes.said: FY25 consolidated forecast 'recently' published on SAM.gov
reviewNotes.found: The FY25 forecast notice dates to 2024, so it is stale. DIA posted a separate special notice (DF-0001-26) in July 2026. Look on SAM.gov for an FY26/FY27 forecast from the Virginia Contracting Activity.
reviewNotes.action: Search SAM.gov API for Federal Organization 97DL special notices. Added 7 DIA rows from the OSBP page: NeedipeDIA, forecast/industry days, OSBP briefings, SIA 3, SITE III, DoDIIS, Mentor-Protégé.

reviewNotes.found: Both URLs are right. The NRO site is the Acquisition Research Center (ARC), run by the ACE. NSA ARC requires registration and blocks access from government computers. Neither has an API.
reviewNotes.action: Register both company accounts; track manually.

reviewNotes.said: Uses BAAs; active programs BENGAL, HAYSTAC, WRIVA, End-Gen, COSMIC, AGILE
reviewNotes.found: Missing the biggest new IARPA pathway: the IARPA Solutions Marketplace (IARPA-OT-26-001), a rolling open-call OT running Aug 1, 2026 – Jul 31, 2027 with monthly cut-offs. The listed programs are research programs, mostly already under way, not open calls.
reviewNotes.action: Add the Marketplace to the pipeline; treat program names as targets for teaming, not open solicitations.

reviewNotes.said: Albatross UAS, Intrinsic Market Resilience, Atomically Precise Molecules, Flexoelectric Future RFI
reviewNotes.found: Not re-verified in this pass. DARPA has no API, but every solicitation posts to SAM.gov/Grants.gov.
reviewNotes.action: Pull live DARPA notices from the SAM.gov API instead of maintaining a manual list.

reviewNotes.said: Robotics anytime; MRI and STC deadlines early 2027
reviewNotes.found: Deadlines not re-verified. NSF's own API covers past awards only; open opportunities come through Grants.gov.
reviewNotes.action: Use Grants.gov API (agency NSF) for open calls; NSF Award API for sponsor intel.

reviewNotes.said: DEFENSEWERX and NSIN post challenges on their own sites
reviewNotes.found: Correct in principle. The PIA list is larger: DoD-wide PIAs TechLink and MilTech, Griffiss Institute, VT-ARC BRICC, DOE's ENERGYWERX/TechWerx/ConnectWerx, and DHS's DEFENSEWERX, MilTech and RTI. NSIN's current status was not re-verified.
reviewNotes.action: Add the extra PIAs to monitoring; confirm NSIN is still active.

reviewNotes.found: Consortia are the main OT channel. DoD obligated over $24B in consortia OTAs in FY2019–2021. Most require paid membership to see requests.
reviewNotes.action: Pick 2–3 consortia that match Forge's focus and join; ATI's active-solicitations page covers many at once.

reviewNotes.found: Only a handful of sources have true APIs: SAM.gov, Grants.gov / Simpler.Grants.gov, SBIR.gov, USAspending, Federal Register (plus NIH RSS and the NSF/NIH award APIs). Together they capture almost every formal solicitation, including DARPA, IARPA, DIA and DIU notices. Everything else (PIAs, consortia, IC portals, marketplaces) has to be watched by page monitoring or membership.
